# P03 Regulatory Gap Analysis: Cris Santos Company | Wholesale Trade | Multi-Sector

| | |
|---|---|
| Scope at this tier | Each division's primary regulation plus group-wide obligations |
| Expected depth | Regulation-by-division matrix |
| Deliverable form | Gap tables per division plus group roadmap |
| Universal method | [P03_regulatory-gap-analysis/README.md](../../../../00_universal/projects/P03_regulatory-gap-analysis/README.md) |
| Scenario brief | [README.md](../README.md) |

**Regulation to analyze:** NIST SP 800-171 R2 via CMMC Level 2 / DFARS 252.204-7012, 32 CFR 170.14; 48 CFR 252.204-7012
**Why:** For supply-chain-focused wholesalers, the most prescriptive, auditable and contractually enforced US control set is NIST SP 800-171 R2 (110 requirements) as required by DFARS 7012 and assessed under CMMC Level 2 (Phase 1 live since Nov 10, 2025). It flows down to subcontractors and distributors handling CUI. Wholesalers with no federal/defense business should instead use CISA CPGs 2.0 / NIST CSF 2.0 plus CTPAT MSC cybersecurity criteria as the benchmark, because no sector-wide federal cyber rule applies to wholesale trade.
